tls:text.tls:line: He would make his plans with greater aims in mind.40 40 The reference is to Zuozhuan, Lord Xuan, Year 12; also Lord Zhao, Year 22, in which xian 鮮 means “fresh game” or “spoils” of the hunt or an expedition. Wen Ying (Hanshu 62.2734) reads xian as ming 明 (clear): “He would make his plans when the situation is clear.” Wu Kaisheng suggests that xian 鮮 may be a loan word for xian 先 (cited in Gao 1990, 101): “He would make his plans ahead of time.” This passage my also allude to General Li Guang, who committed suicide rather than respond to the judicial officials (Shiji 109.2876).
